summary: WebSocket H2->H1 upgrade via edge proxy inserts chunked framing and causes midstream event reordering and truncated final event
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-running WebSocket streaming calls intermittently return a truncated final event (missing closing JSON metadata) and duplicated intermediate chunks after the client crosses a network path that triggers their CDN/edge to re-establish connections.

Impact:
- Production traffic for BrightFlow's realtime summarization pipeline shows ~1.2% of streams ending without finalization; customer must request a re-run.
- Blocks BrightFlow from rolling to GA; customer escalated to enterprise support.

Environment:
- Client: BrightFlow web-app using SDK-js v2.2.0 with subprotocol "redwood-stream-v2"
- Edge: customer routed through FastEdge CDN -> our edge-proxy (h2 terminated) -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime
- Occurs in prod (us-west primary) and sporadically in eu-central during cross-region failover

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start a long streaming generation (~1k tokens).
2) Induce network path change (client sim: switch wifi -> cellular or simulate CDN warm-up that causes HTTP/2 connection migration).
3) Client reconnects using the same session token; SDK attempts upgrade/hand-off.
4) Stream sometimes emits duplicated midstream tokens and the final "end" event is truncated (missing closing metadata JSON).

Observed behaviour:
- Sequence numbers out of order in received frames (e.g., chunk 102 appears after 115).
- Final frame arrives with incomplete JSON (truncated trailing "]" and metadata fields).
- Logs from our edge-proxy show an injected "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" header on the proxied upgrade path, followed by odd chunk-size boundaries logged during the same timeframe.

Expected behaviour:
- Upgraded WebSocket stream should preserve ordering and deliver a finalization event with full metadata consistently after reconnect/hand-off.

Logs & artifacts attached in ticket: trace ids (edge / gw): EDGE-202602-04A, GW-202602-04B, client-sample HAR and SDK debug capture.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Client-side: enable SDK retry-on-incomplete-final (workaround flag) and short-circuit to non-streaming fallback for long-running sessions until fix deployed.
- Customer applied the workaround and saw reduction in visible failures but still requests a platform-side fix.
comments: 2026-02-15 10:12 UTC — Ryan (Support): Acknowledged. Repro steps received from BrightFlow. Tagging SRE + Edge team. SLA P1 acknowledged.

2026-02-15 11:05 UTC — Priya (SRE): Captured edge-proxy logs for trace EDGE-202602-04A. Noted 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' appears on proxied upgrade in same 5s window as sequence misordering. Attaching packet reassembly logs. Hypothesis: proxy is mixing chunked framing with websocket frame stream when handling http/2->http/1 handoff.

2026-02-15 13:40 UTC — Miguel (Edge): Reproduced with internal harness against FastEdge emulation. Observed chunk-size boundaries injected by our http/1 adapter inside the handoff code path. Filing PR to remove TE header injection for upgrade requests. See PR #987.
2026-02-15 16:20 UTC — BrightFlow (Customer): We applied SDK flag and saw failures drop from 1.2% to ~0.2%. Appreciate ETA on platform patch; critical for our GA next week.

2026-02-16 09:00 UTC — Miguel (Edge): Hotfix deployed to edge-proxy Canary (version edge-proxy 1.8.3-hotfix). Verified canary streams with simulated handoff no longer show injected TE header and ordering appears stable in test harness. Rolling to prod in us-west at 13:00 UTC.
investigation_notes: Checked upstream: FastEdge sometimes downgrades h2 connection to h1 on warm-up. Our h1 adapter previously added Transfer-Encoding: chunked for streamed responses; this interferes with WebSocket frame passthrough during upgrade handoffs.
Reproducer: internal harness that toggles protocol version and simulates keepalive/handshake yielded deterministic reordering when TE header present.

Captured binary frame deltas: mismatch occurs where chunk size delimiter bytes are interpreted as part of next websocket frame payload on client-side parser implementations that expect contiguous frames.

Correlated customer SDK logs: when duplicate midstream tokens appear the SDK shows a short gap (~80ms) followed by a replayed buffer; suggests partial reassembly after chunk boundary is handled incorrectly.

Related previous ticket: SUP-314159 (socket-handoff-incomplete-terminal-json-batch) — similar symptom but root cause there was LB connection reuse; here root cause is explicit TE injection on upgrade path.
Mitigation validated: disabling TE injection + ensuring upgrade requests bypass streaming-chunking logic prevents corruption in all simulated handoff cases.
resolution_notes: Root cause: edge-proxy http/1 adapter was adding Transfer-Encoding: chunked for proxied responses and in a small race this corrupted websocket upgrade passthrough during path migration, resulting in interleaved chunk delimiters being interpreted as part of the websocket payload by certain clients.

Fix deployed: edge-proxy PR #987 removed TE injection for 'Upgrade: websocket' proxied requests and added explicit passthrough mode for h2->h1 handoff. Canary rolled at 2026-02-16 06:00 UTC, full prod roll-out completed in us-west 2026-02-16 13:25 UTC. eu-central scheduled 2026-02-17 03:00 UTC.
Customer action: BrightFlow reverted SDK workaround flag and confirmed streams finalize correctly in us-west after canary/prod rollout. They observed failures drop to 0.05% (within noise).

Follow-ups created: INT-33091: add e2e handoff tests for websocket upgrade scenarios (http/2->http/1/CDN), INT-33102: update runbook and add alert for TE header seen on Upgrade requests, DOC-1222: release note for SDK mentioning edge-proxy fix and recommended SDK version 2.3.1.
Closure: Recommend leaving ticket open for 72h of customer-observed stability after eu-central rollout, then mark Resolved.
